questions.q: How many containers does a real data lake design typically use?
options: Usually few, sometimes just one — directories do most of the real organizing
One container per file, always
As many as possible, for maximum organization
Exactly twelve, one per month
questions.explain: Containers are a heavier, more fixed unit than directories, so most designs minimize how many they use.

questions.q: What determines the file format used at each zone in a data lake path?
options: Raw zones usually keep the original source format; anything meant for real analysis gets converted to Parquet or Delta
Every zone must use the exact same file format with no exceptions
File format is chosen randomly per file
Only JSON is allowed anywhere in a data lake
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 8's format tradeoffs applied practically across a real pipeline.

questions.q: In the five-decision framework, how should access typically be granted?
options: Broad RBAC roles for the team on the whole account, with ACLs reserved for genuine exceptions on specific directories
Every single directory needs its own separate ACL, with RBAC never used
Access should never be restricted in a data lake
Only SAS tokens should ever be used, never RBAC or ACLs
questions.explain: This directly reflects Lesson 5's guidance: RBAC for broad access, ACLs for exceptions.

questions.q: Why does hierarchical namespace (Lessons 2 and 4) have to be decided before any of this design work starts?
options: Every one of the five design decisions assumes real directories exist to organize around
Hierarchical namespace has no real connection to data lake design
It only matters for security, not for directory structure
It can be enabled at any point without affecting the design
questions.explain: Without real directory objects, the entire zone/source/partition structure this lesson describes wouldn't be possible.

questions.q: In the example path, what does 'year=2024/month=01/' represent?
options: A Hive-style partition, from Lesson 9, matching how the data will actually be queried
A container name
A file format designation
An RBAC role assignment
questions.explain: This is the same Hive-style partitioning convention covered in Lesson 9, applied inside a real directory structure.
